meta.description: Single source of truth for WHERE every compliance document lives across the codebase (git), Google Drive, and Notion - its canonical home, its mirrors, its owner, its review dates, and which compliance bundles it belongs to. This is the document-level analogue of audit-reports/FINDINGS.json (which tracks finding status). The codebase copy is canonical; the Notion board is a one-way mirror; Drive docs are referenced by URL, never copied. See docs/legal/COMPLIANCE_DOCS_GUIDE.md.
meta.idAlgorithm: id = 'DOC-' + sha256(canonicalLocation) first 10 hex chars; stable across runs so a moved/renamed doc reads as a diff. Computed and written back by scripts/document-register-render.rb.
meta.contentHashNote: contentHash is sha256 of the canonical content. For canonicalSystem=git rows the render script computes it from the file bytes at its repo path and CI verifies it in --check (a tracked doc edited without updating its row fails). For drive/notion rows the hash is externally supplied: Notion-row hashes can be refreshed automatically by the network-capable Notion-sync run (--refresh-notion-hashes); DRIVE-row hashes have NO automated refresh and must be supplied by the operator (the sync script carries no Google credentials), so Drive freshness is a dated review obligation, not an automated guarantee. CI is network-free: a null/empty drive/notion hash is allowed and surfaced as an advisory, never a CI failure.
meta.governance: Only Scot changes a document's attestation, or moves its status to approved/published. The compliance-officer agent and the main session keep the index current (add/retire rows, refresh review dates, maintain bundles and contentHash) but never attest. Drafts stay status:draft with an empty attestation until Scot signs. No student/patient data ever appears here; entries are titles, paths/URLs, and hashes only.

meta.retentionNote: EVERY retention block is status:draft and legally inert. Nothing in this register wires, schedules, or authorises deletion. --check performs SHAPE validation only: required fields present, class resolves to meta.retentionSchedule, and the row's denormalised rule/disposition match that schedule entry. dispositionEligibleAfter MUST stay null while retention.status is not "approved" - --check enforces that, so a draft schedule can never produce a disposition date. Only Scot moves a retention rule to approved, and only after counsel review. retention.ambiguous:true marks a row whose class was inferred rather than read off the sec 5.2 table; those are the rows counsel should look at first. Note also that no current row carries a delete disposition: where sec 5.2 was ambiguous the assignment was made conservatively toward archive, so the delete-disposition classes exist in the schedule with zero members.
meta.supersessionNote: supersedes / supersededBy form a two-way chain and --check enforces reciprocity: if A.supersededBy == B then B.supersedes must == A, neither may self-reference, both ids must resolve to real rows, and a row carrying supersededBy must have status:superseded. Attestation freezes bytes: a superseded record is never edited, renamed, or moved - it keeps its row, its title, and its bundle membership in any frozen point-in-time binder, and only the pointer is added.
meta.driveFileIdNote: driveFileId is the stable Google Drive file ID, required on every canonicalSystem=drive row and forbidden on git/notion rows. Drive IDs survive renames and moves; path-shaped URLs do not. --check verifies the id is the one embedded in canonicalLocation, so the two can never disagree.
meta.completenessNote: Register/reality drift is checked in both directions. Registered-but-missing has always been a hard failure (a git row must resolve to a real in-repo file). Present-but-unregistered is now checked too: every tracked file under docs/legal/ must have a git row or --check fails, because that directory is unambiguously the compliance corpus. The .claude/agents/ sweep is advisory only, since that directory also holds non-compliance agents. Drive and Notion completeness cannot be checked here (CI is network-free) and remains a dated review obligation.

meta.bundleMatchNote: bundleDefinitions[*].requiredDocs binds each requirement to a specific document by canonicalLocation (identity), not free-text title, so a doc retitled to a required string cannot satisfy a requirement. Each requiredDoc carries a human-readable title that --check verifies still matches the member at that location (register-drift guard). --check fails if a requiredDoc location is not a bundle member, or its title has drifted.
meta.bundleGapNote: bundleDefinitions[*].gaps names artifacts a bundle genuinely needs that DO NOT EXIST as records yet. A gap is a deliberate, visible hole: it is rendered in DOCUMENT-REGISTER.md and never satisfied by inventing a row or by pointing a requiredDoc at an unrelated document. gaps never fail --check; an unmet requiredDoc always does. Close a gap by creating the real artifact and promoting it out of gaps into requiredDocs.
meta.integrityNote: --check also enforces: every canonicalSystem is one of canonicalSystemEnum; a git row canonicalLocation is a repo path (not a URL); a drive/notion row canonicalLocation is a URL and does not resolve to a tracked repo file (so a git doc cannot dodge hash verification by being relabeled drive/notion); and id + canonicalLocation are unique across the register.
meta.attestationHashNote: attestation.attestedContentHash pins the sha256 of the bytes that were actually attested, alongside contentHash which tracks the file as it is now. document-register-render.rb --check fails when the two diverge on a canonicalSystem=git row: the attested revision no longer exists and re-attestation is owed. Enforced for git rows only - Drive and Notion hashes are operator-supplied with no automated refresh, so the field is rejected there. Render NEVER backfills this field; populating it from current bytes would make every attestation self-certifying. Only Scot attests, and the hash is pinned when the attestation is recorded.
meta.attestationBackfillNote: CLEARED 2026-07-23. All seven rows that predated the attestedContentHash check were re-attested against their current revisions and now pin their attested bytes, so the grandfather list is empty and every attested git row is verifiable. It stays empty: the closed set in scripts/document-register-render.rb is the ceiling and nothing is ever added to it, so a future attestation must pin its hash when it is recorded.
meta.legalNamingNote: CLOSED set of docs/legal records whose names predate the statusless dated naming rule (docs/legal/README.md, "Naming"). They keep their names because renaming breaks every inbound reference for no compliance benefit. scripts/legal-naming-check.rb treats any git-canonical docs/legal row that is neither dated nor listed here as a NEW violation, and treats a listed path that is no longer a row as a stale entry to remove. This list may only SHRINK. Note there is deliberately NO exemption list for the four grandfathered dated _draft records: the status-token check fires only on rows that carry an attestation, so their exemption expires automatically the moment one is attested.

documents.notes: Path A successor to DOC-6d37a68cf4 (attested 2026-08-19), created 2026-08-25. Corrects an ENFORCEMENT claim, not a compliance one: purge_old_eu_logs! deletes jurisdiction = 'EU' AND created_at < 5.years.ago (app/models/ai_api_log.rb:244-248); the jurisdiction column was created 2026-06-21 (db/migrate/20260621120000_add_article_50_fields_to_ai_api_logs.rb), so the oldest possible stamped row turns five years old on 2031-06-21 and the job matches zero rows until then. Two carriers: the attestation-history narrative (:36, PR #656 moved "the EU tier from inert to functional") and the section 6 retention table (:293). No data was retained longer than a rule permits; this is an enforcement-description defect, not a retention violation. The defect is that a document offered as evidence described a dormant job as an operating control. The same claim was corrected in place in the unattested draft docs/legal/2026-08-09_data-retention_draft.md (DOC-e62caf7fb9), which needed no supersession. NOTE ON LEGAL BASIS (added 2026-08-25 after review): the predecessor's "Basis" column attributes this tier to "EU AI Act Article 50 record-keeping". That attribution is INHERITED, not endorsed here, and is flagged as an open question for counsel: Article 50 is the AI Act's transparency provision and nothing in this record establishes that it imposes a five-year AiApiLog retention duty. This correction is scoped to the ENFORCEMENT claim only and takes no position on the legal basis. WINDOW CLAIM, tightened 2026-08-25 after review: the binding fact is the TABLE's age, not the stamp. ai_api_logs was created 2026-02-21 (db/migrate/20260221000001_create_ai_api_logs.rb), so no row can be five years old before 2031-02-21; write-time-stamped rows cannot qualify before 2031-06-21. A backfill or manual UPDATE stamping older rows could make one eligible sooner; no such backfill exists (no update_all touching jurisdiction). The earlier phrasing "cannot delete any row before 2031-06-21" was an overstatement. OPERATIVE REASON, added 2026-08-25 after review: the date is not why it matches nothing. The stamp writes 'EU' only for a confirmed :eu user (lib/eu_jurisdiction.rb; :unknown and :non_eu both map to nil), and as of the 2026-08-23 read EuJurisdiction.status is :unknown for 34 of 34 production accounts with jurisdiction null on all 64 AiApiLog rows. Nothing has ever been stamped, so the control is structurally dormant rather than merely date-gated; it does not start working in 2031 by the passage of time. ALIGNED 2026-08-26 after external review: an earlier phrasing here called the control "structurally dormant", which overstated it. spec/models/ai_api_log_spec.rb:550-586 drives a real EU user through the resolver and the purge deletes the row, so the mechanism is verified end to end. Zero production matches reflect an absence of eligible DATA (no confirmed :eu user; no row five years old), not a broken control. What the predecessor got wrong is that it matches EU rows in production today.
